terms.meaning: Optical character recognition: software that reads text from a photo or scan.
A value passed in the web address of a screen, here the document ID.
A shared place in the app where data such as scan results is kept and changed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the parts the screen needs: layout pieces, icons, navigation, shared colours and spacing, shared buttons and cards, the document store, and the data type definitions for prescriptions.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup so the screen can use the shared look and the shared data.

sections.name: PrescriptionReviewScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the scan and changing the medicine list
sections.what: Reads the document ID, fetches the scan result when the screen opens, and handles adding, editing and saving medicines. If loading fails, the user can enter details by hand or go back.
sections.why: Likely reason: the screen needs the scan data before it can show anything, and a fallback is offered when that fails.
sections.watch_out: Edits exist only on this screen until Done is pressed, so leaving early loses them.

sections.name: PrescriptionReviewScreen: if
sections.title: Waiting view, header and doctor details
sections.what: Shows a spinner with the message that the AI is analysing the prescription. Once loaded, shows the top bar with a close button and a Done button, a banner with the average AI confidence, and editable boxes for doctor name and diagnosis.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells the user the AI is working and shows how confident it is, before the user checks the details.
sections.watch_out: The banner shows only an average, so one unreliable medicine can be hidden behind a high overall number.

sections.name: PrescriptionReviewScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Medicine list and removal
sections.what: Shows a heading with the number of medicines and a plus button to add one. Each medicine appears as a card with an editable name and a bin button that removes it.
sections.why: Likely reason: each medicine is editable on its own, so the user can fix one without retyping the rest.
sections.watch_out: The bin button removes the medicine straight away, with no confirmation.

sections.name: PrescriptionReviewScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Dosage, timing and duration fields
sections.what: For each medicine, three small editable boxes for dosage, timing (for example twice a day) and duration, and at the bottom a Confirm and Save button.
sections.why: Likely reason: these three details are what reminders are built from.
sections.watch_out: Timing is free text, so the app cannot check that it is a valid schedule before saving.

sections.name: PrescriptionReviewScreen (part 5)
sections.title: Styles for the review screen
sections.what: Holds the look settings for this screen: cards, input boxes, buttons, spacing and text sizes. Changing a value here only changes appearance.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps look settings in one place at the bottom of the file.
sections.watch_out: Some values are typed in directly rather than taken from the shared theme, so a theme change may miss them.

summary: Lets a user check and correct the list of medicines that the app read from a prescription photo, then save it.
purpose: Gives a person a chance to fix scanning mistakes such as wrong medicine names or doses before the prescription and its reminders are stored.
why: Likely reason: automatic reading makes mistakes and medical details must be confirmed by a person. The confidence score is shown so the user knows where to look harder.
how: When the screen opens it reads the document ID from the route, asks the document store for the scan result, and shows a spinner while waiting. Then it shows editable boxes for doctor name and diagnosis, followed by one editable card for each medicine. Changes are kept in a local copy on the screen. Pressing Done or Confirm and Save sends that copy to the store to be saved, then shows a success message and returns to the home tab.
inputs: The document ID from the route, the scan result from getOcrResult in the document store, and whatever the user types or removes.
outputs: A saved prescription through confirmPrescription, a success or failure alert, and navigation back to the home tab.
risks: Edits are lost if the user leaves before saving. Removing a medicine has no undo. A medicine with a blank name can be saved. Both Done and Confirm and Save save the same data. When the scan fails, the screen offers manual entry, which starts with an empty list. The failure message on save gives no reason.
debug: If the spinner never stops, check getOcrResult in documentStore and the server response for this document. If saving always fails, check confirmPrescription and the network call it makes. If values look wrong on screen, compare the scan result data with what is displayed.
